title: India Finish Eighth at Hockey World Cup After Shootout Heartbreak Against Belgium
excerpt: Harmanpreet Singh's last-second equalizer forces shootout, but Belgium hold nerve to claim 4-3 victory in classification match
body:
• India lost 3-4 to Belgium in a penalty shootout after a dramatic 3-3 draw, finishing eighth at the FIH Men's Hockey World Cup 2026
  • Captain Harmanpreet Singh scored twice — including a last-second penalty corner equalizer — to finish with eight tournament goals, joint-top scorer alongside Argentina's Domene
  • India's worst World Cup finish since 2014 raises urgent questions ahead of the 2027 Asian Games, with only two wins from six matches in the tournament

India's Men's Hockey World Cup 2026 campaign ended in heartbreak on Friday as Belgium edged them 4-3 in a penalty shootout following a gripping 3-3 draw in the 7th/8th place classification match at the Belfius Hockey Arena in Wavre.

The result means India finish eighth — their joint-worst placement at a World Cup — having managed only two wins and seven points from six matches across the tournament co-hosted by Belgium and the Netherlands.

A Match of Momentum Swings

India started brightly. In the sixth minute, Manpreet Singh found Abhishek at a tight angle, and the forward's powerful push beat Belgian goalkeeper Vincent Vanasch, who could only pad the ball into his own net.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=tZWamo-4uZY

The lead lasted until the second quarter, when Belgium turned the screw. Captain Harmanpreet Singh's yellow card for India having an extra player on the pitch gave Belgium a numerical advantage they exploited relentlessly. Goalkeeper Suraj Karkera produced three saves from Alexander Hendrickx's penalty corner drag-flicks during this period, but Belgium broke through regardless.

Roman Duvekot equalized in the 22nd minute, creating space after receiving a cross and wrong-footing two Indian defenders. Barely a minute later, Hugo Labouchere converted a penalty corner to put the hosts 2-1 ahead at half-time.

"We had a rough start. It was a game of two halves."

— Craig Fulton, India Men's Hockey Team Head Coach

Harmanpreet's Heroics

India responded immediately after the break. Rajinder Singh helped earn a penalty corner, and Harmanpreet's trademark drag-flick beat Vanasch to make it 2-2. Belgium challenged the goal via video review, but the equalizer stood.

The third quarter ended level, but Belgium regained the lead early in the fourth period. Nicolas de Kerpel's shot bounced off the turf past goalkeeper Mohith HS after the ball struck an Indian defender, restoring Belgium's advantage at 3-2.

With time running out and India trailing, coach Craig Fulton pulled goalkeeper Karkera for an extra outfield player with less than three minutes remaining. The gamble paid off. India won a penalty corner with just 26 seconds on the clock, and Harmanpreet delivered once again, beating Vanasch to force a shootout.

Shootout Heartbreak

Belgium held their nerve in the shootout. Tom Boon, Arthur de Sloover, and Alexander Hendrickx (via penalty stroke) all converted before Roman Duvekot sealed the decisive fourth goal — despite India's Mohith contesting with a referral that was ultimately rejected.

For India, Harmanpreet and Sukhjeet Singh were both denied by Vanasch, while Shilanand Lakra, Dilpreet Singh, and Abhishek converted their attempts, leaving India one short at 3-4.

Tournament in Review

Harmanpreet Singh's eight goals across the tournament placed him joint-top of the scoring charts alongside Argentina's Domene. But individual brilliance could not mask systemic problems. India finished bottom of Pool E after losses to the Netherlands (1-3) and Argentina (3-5), exiting the semi-final race early.

The eighth-place finish is India's worst at a World Cup since 2014 and a stark contrast to their bronze medal at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021 and silver at the 2023 Asian Games. For the Indian hockey community worldwide — which rallied behind the team during the Olympics resurgence — the result is a sobering reality check.

Road Ahead

With the Asian Games approaching, India must address their defensive vulnerabilities and inconsistent penalty corner conversion. The attacking intent has been visible in patches throughout the tournament, but translating that into sustained four-quarter performances remains the central challenge for Fulton's squad.
